forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: The council says it continues to buy additional temporary accommodation to manage increasing homelessness demand, with the Temporary Accommodation capital budget revised from £2.0m to £3.2m.
findings.detail: The paper reports that Housing Options is breakeven at Q2, and that temporary accommodation purchases are helping to manage demand. It also reports the Renters Rights Act and the in-sourcing of Home-Move as pressures being monitored.
findings.matters: Rising temporary accommodation demand is a growing budget pressure for councils with housing duties, and the capital purchases needed to meet it add to borrowing needs.
findings.figures: £2.0m original Temporary Accommodation capital budget; £3.2m revised budget at Q2; Housing Options breakeven at Q2
findings.quote: The purchase of additional temporary accommodation continues to help manage increasing demand.

findings.headline: The Government paused and is reviewing the national Local Government Reorganisation programme on 7 September 2026, with no revised timetable.
findings.detail: The paper says the review includes all outstanding decisions, including West Sussex, and that local elections in May 2027 will proceed on existing boundaries. The council says it continues to incur resource costs for preparedness, programme management and transition planning.
findings.matters: A council carrying LGR preparation costs with no timetable is holding an unresolved cost base, which matters to finance officers at other councils in reorganisation areas.
findings.figures: No cost figure given in this paper
findings.quote: On 7 September 2026, the Government announced a pause and review of the national Local Government Reorganisation programme

findings.headline: Digital and Technology reports a £17k overspend at Q2, against breakeven at Q1, linked to ICT cost inflation.
findings.detail: The paper attributes the pressure to Uniform iDox migration costs, employee budget pressures and ICT-related cost increases. It says ICT markets face double-digit inflation in cloud software subscriptions and higher PC prices, and that the impact depends on contracts and renewal dates.
findings.matters: The paper links a small overspend to specific supplier price pressures, which other councils with cloud and ICT contracts will recognise.
findings.figures: £17k overspend Digital and Technology (Q1 breakeven); 'double-digit inflation' in cloud software subscriptions
findings.quote: the service is reporting an overspend £17k (Q1 breakeven)

findings.headline: Mid Sussex cuts its 2026/27 capital spend plan from £13.7m to £10.4m, reprofiling a net £3.279m into later years.
findings.detail: The paper says the review moved the Second Depot construction phase to spring 2027 (£2.000m) and spread the Parks Improvements budget over three years (£1.429m). Delivery of ICT Strategy works, brought forward into 2026/27, offsets £0.150m.
findings.matters: Slippage of this size on a £13.7m programme is a signal to finance officers and lenders about delivery capacity and the timing of borrowing needs.
findings.figures: £13.7m original 2026/27 plan; £10.4m revised 2026/27 forecast; £3.279m net reprofiled; £2.000m Second Depot; £1.429m Parks Improvements; £(0.150m) ICT Strategy brought forward
findings.quote: the annual spend for 2026/27 is now planned to be £10.4m

findings.headline: Q2 treasury receipts of £976k are allocated £500k to a Place Regeneration Reserve and £410k to General Reserve, with a £66k Election Reserve transfer.
findings.detail: The paper proposes setting the receipts aside for regeneration projects, with the remainder going to General Reserve. The Q2 table also shows a £66k transfer to the Election Reserve for the May 2027 district election, and Q1 transfers of £215k each to the Process & Efficiency Reserve and General Reserve.
findings.matters: Building reserves from treasury income, and earmarking part of it for regeneration, shows how a council is using a non-recurring windfall ahead of a forecast gap.
findings.figures: £500k Place Regeneration Reserve; £410k General Reserve (Q2); £215k General Reserve (Q1); £215k Process & Efficiency Reserve; £66k Election Reserve; £1,406k total allocated
findings.quote: it is proposed that these receipts be set aside for regeneration projects
